name: NTEN homepage: the Nonprofit Technology Network's membership landing page
title: NTEN homepage: the Nonprofit Technology Network's membership landing page
answer: NTEN, the Nonprofit Technology Network, publishes this page as its organizational homepage, a membership and community landing page rather than a research report. Its most useful content for an AI reader is the framing it states plainly: nonprofit technology is marked by inequities within organizations and the sector that must be dismantled, and users, builders and funders all share responsibility for equitable technology use. The page offers no survey data, no dates and no AI policy findings, so it points to NTEN's research rather than reporting it.

sections.body: NTEN, the Nonprofit Technology Network, publishes this page as its organizational homepage. It is a membership and community landing page rather than a research report, and it carries no publication date. Its scope is promotional and programmatic: it describes NTEN's mission, its community, its job board, its awards, its committees, its membership benefits, its professional certificates and scholarships, and its Equity Guide pledge. The page does not present survey findings, methodology or data.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page states NTEN's purpose as creating a world where missions and movements are successful through the skillful and equitable use of technology. It invites readers to join a nonprofit community of people who want to put technology to work for social change, and it says nonprofit technology is marked by inequities within organizations and the sector that must be dismantled if communities' needs are to be addressed permanently. It addresses users, builders and funders, saying each has a responsibility to ensure the equitable use of technology. It offers ways to take part: finding full-time or short-term work at a nonprofit or other organization using technology for social change, joining committees on accessibility, equity and programs, becoming a member for professional development and discounts, earning a professional certificate, applying for scholarships for a course or certificate when finances are tight, pledging to use the Equity Guide, and celebrating software developers who create open source apps and tools that nonprofit and advocacy groups can put to good use. The page repeats its community invitation twice.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives no numbers, no dates, no survey results and no definitions beyond its own mission statement, and it names no research reports. The only positions it states are that nonprofit technology is marked by inequities within organizations and the sector that must be dismantled, and that users, builders and funders share responsibility for the equitable use of technology.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in nonprofits would use this page as a pointer to the organization, not as evidence. The industry page cites NTEN for sector-wide research on technology investment, digital maturity and AI policy adoption, but this harvested text contains none of that. What it does show is the framing NTEN applies to technology work, equity, access and community, which is the lens the organization says it brings to the sector. Anyone wanting the survey findings must go to NTEN's research publications rather than this homepage.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Nonprofits

sections.body: This is a landing page with little substance. It contains no research findings, no methodology, no sample sizes, no dates and no AI-specific content. It is promotional in tone and commercial in the sense that it advertises membership, certificates and scholarships. It is undated, so a reader cannot tell how current it is, and it is partial, covering only what NTEN chooses to put on its front page.
